Hi Alyssa —

Appreciate the quick read-through. High level answers below — pulling Kimberly in for legal/tax confirmation.

- Invoice cutover / first invoice: We can set activation on 2025-10-01. First invoice would be generated on 2025-10-05 and cover the activation fee + prorated usage for October. We do prorate by calendar days for activation months.
- Proration details: activation fee is not prorated; usage is prorated based on seconds of service. We can add explicit language to the order form to avoid ambiguity.
- Net terms / payable name: Redwood accepts Net-30 by default for this deal. Invoice remit: Redwood, Inc. — 123 Redwood Way, San Francisco, CA 94105. Payable to: Redwood, Inc. Wire/ACH instructions will be on the invoice stub. If procurement requires Net-45 we can review but Net-30 is standard for pilots.
- Tax allocation: Redwood will not gross-up for withholding. For US/Canada: we need Stella to provide tax ID(s) and indicate which entity will receive invoices. If sales tax/VAT evidence is needed for Canada, please include the tax registration certificate. Kimberly — can you confirm whether we should add a clause that places VAT/responsibility on the buyer with required evidence?

Next steps: I can produce a short exhibit to the order form with the cutover date, proration table, and remit instructions and share for sign-off. Should I proceed?

Hi Alyssa / Ben —

Thanks for the context. I reviewed the attached draft and sketched targeted redlines to avoid downstream disputes. Key items we propose (summary):

- Net terms: keep Net-30 in the order form but add a clause allowing Redwood to move to Net-45 for customers that request extended credit terms; any change requires written notice 30 days prior to the next invoice.
- Proration & activation: explicit table for activation fee (flat, not prorated) and prorated usage calculation (daily pro-rata formula).
- Tax language: buyer-responsible for all applicable taxes, duties and withholdings. Buyer must supply tax registration evidence for non-US taxes within 10 business days of execution. If buyer requests Redwood to gross-up or withhold differently, a written payment instruction and indemnity from buyer is required.
- Invoice remit: redact legal name and remit address to match Redwood legal entity. Add a PO field on the invoice template; if PO is not provided within 10 business days of execution, invoices will be issued to the primary billing contact and payment terms still apply.

I've attached the redline (redlined_orderform_kp.pdf) with inline edits and suggested language. Two asks for Stella:
  * Confirm the exact legal entity name and tax ID for US and Canada.
  * Confirm AP contact and desired PO format.

If those are confirmed we can produce a clean final order form and circulate for signature (DocuSign). Ben — if you want, I can incorporate the exhibit with activation dates and remit details and circulate the final PDF today.

Regards,
